items.label: text
items.text: This question is about copper(ll) sulfate solution.

items.label: list_item
items.text: a Describe a procedure to make a solution of copper(ll) sulfate starting from copper(Il) oxide. (ε)

items.label: list_item
items.text: b Describe a chemical test that can be used to show that the solution

items.label: list_item
items.text: contains sulfate ions. (2)

items.label: list_item
items.text: c A student added some sodium hydroxide solution to the copper(Il) sulfate solution. State the name of the blue precipitate formed. (1)

items.label: list_item
items.text: d A student carried out an experiment to investigate displacement reactions of three different metals with copper(ll) sulfate solution. She followed this method:

items.label: list_item
items.text: Put some copper(ll) sulfate solution into a polystyrene cup.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Measure the initial temperature.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Add some metal.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Stir the solution.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Record the maximum temperature.

items.label: list_item
items.text: The student uses the same amount in moles of each metal in the experiments. State two other variables the student should keep the same in this experiment to allow her to be able to compare the different metals.

items.label: list_item
items.text: ii The student recorded the following data.

items.label: table
items.text:
| Metal   |   Temperature change/°C |
|---------|-------------------------|
| zinc    |                      15 |
| silver  |                       0 |
| nickel  |                       7 |

items.label: text
items.text: Arrange the four metals, zinc, silver, copper and nickel, in order of reactivity, starting with the most reactive. (1)

items.label: list_item
items.text: iii The student did not carry out the experiment with copper and copper(ll) sulfate. Predict, giving a reason, what the temperature rise would be for this experiment. (2)

items.label: list_item
items.text: iv The student carried out the experiment using 3.25g of zinc (0.05 mol). She then used the same amount in moles of nickel and silver. Another student decided to use the same mass (3.25g) of each metal. The results of the two students were very similar. Suggest reasons for this. (ε)

items.label: list_item
items.text: V The ionic equation for the reaction between copper(ll) sulfate solution and nickel is:

items.label: formula
items.text: N i ( s ) + C u ^ { 2 + ( a q ) } \rightarrow N i ^ { 2 + ( a q ) } + C u ( s )

items.label: text
items.text: Use the ionic equation to explain whether nickel is oxidised or reduced in this reaction. (2)

items.label: list_item
items.text: e The student wants to make some anhydrous copper(ll) sulfate. Describe how she could do this starting with copper(ll) sulfate solution. (2)

items.label: list_item
items.text: f The student carried out a flame test on the anhydrous copper(Il) sulfate.

items.label: list_item
items.text: i Describe how to carry out a flame test. (2)

items.label: list_item
items.text: ii State the colour of the flame produced when the student carried out a flame test on copper(Il) sulfate.

items.label: text
items.text: (Total 21 marks)
